name: highwater-too
description: Write screenplays and manuscripts in .highland files, with preview and PDF export, plus a git writing history.

scripts.package: npm run build && node -e "require('fs').copyFileSync('../../LICENSE','LICENSE')" && vsce package --no-dependencies --out ../../highwater-too.vsix

commands.title: Link Writing History to This File
Turn Writing History Off or On for This Document
Open .md Files as Ordinary Markdown Again
Check Spelling While Typing (On or Off)

highwater.historyFolder.markdownDescription: Folder for the writing history (one git repository, a branch per document) and session backups. Empty: the system's place for application data (on a Mac, `~/Library/Application Support/Highwater Too/History`; on Linux, `~/.local/share/highwater-too/history`; on Windows, `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Highwater Too\History`). Use the **Change Writing History Location** command to move it.

highwater.highlandShortcuts.markdownDescription: Writing shortcuts in documents: ⌘E for Preview, ⌘L for Live Margins, ⌘0 for the sidebar, ⌘1 for the Navigator, ⌘2 for the Bin, ⌘4 for Assets and ⌘5 for the Scratchpad and ⇧⌘I for Show Invisibles, instead of VS Code's meanings for those keys. With it off, Preview is ⌃⌥P and Live Margins ⌃⌥L.

highwater.showSidebarOnOpen.markdownDescription: Switch the sidebar to Highwater Too (Navigator, Bin, Assets) when a document is opened in the text editor. (The Highwater Editor has these panels in its own sidebar; VS Code's Highwater Too sidebar closes when it is given focus.)

enumDescriptions: On every computer; double-spaced, so pages hold a line or two more than in the PDF.
The PDF's font, embedded in the file so Word and LibreOffice show it without installing it (Pages and Google Docs do not).

highwater.writingHistory.markdownDescription: Record each save in the writing history (a git repository in the history folder, one branch per document). Needs git (on a Mac, the Xcode command-line tools).

highwater.historyRemote.markdownDescription: Mirror the writing history to this git remote: one repository holding every work, pushed to after saves and never force-pushed. Any host: for example `https://github.com/you/writing-history.git`, `git@gitlab.com:you/history.git` or `ssh://you@server/srv/git/history.git`. Empty: no mirror. Use **Set Up History Mirror…** to set it and create the repository.

highwater.historyMatchMinWords.markdownDescription: A file this computer has no writing history for is recognised as a work in the history when its text is exactly one of that work's saves, but only if it has at least this many words, so empty files and templates never match. (It is always asked before anything is fetched.)

highwater.highlandEditor.markdownDescription: Open screenplays and manuscripts (`.highland`, `.fountain`, and `.md` files Highwater Too handles) in the Highwater Editor. Off: they open as text. Either way, the book and code buttons in the editor's title bar switch a document between the two.

highwater.theme.markdownDescription: Colours for the Highwater Editor and the Navigator: one of its themes, or **Match VS Code**. With `highwater.themeWindow` on, **Choose Theme…** also colours the whole window to match.

highwater.fontSize.markdownDescription: Text size in the Highwater Editor, in pixels. **0** follows VS Code's editor font size, scaled up about 1.4 times. ⌘+ and ⌘− change it; ⌥⌘0 sets it back to 0.

highwater.themeWindow.markdownDescription: When a theme is chosen with **Choose Theme…**, colour the whole VS Code window to match (VS Code's colour theme becomes **Highwater** + the theme's name). **Match VS Code** puts back the colour theme you had before.

highwater.paragraphNumbers.markdownDescription: Show paragraph numbers in the Highwater Editor's margin: every line with text is numbered, except the title page, notes and omitted text on lines of their own, and directives such as `{{HEADER}}` and markers. **Go to Paragraph…** (⌃G) goes to a number.

highwater.spellCheck.markdownDescription: Check spelling as you type in the Highwater Editor, in American English: misspelled words get red dots under them. Right-click one for guesses, **Ignore Spelling** or **Learn Spelling**; ⌘; goes to the next misspelling. Character names (from cues), scene-heading prefixes, directives, addresses and omitted text aren't checked.

highwater.spellingWords.markdownDescription: Words **Learn Spelling** has added to the Highwater Editor's dictionary (any document). Add or remove words here too.

highwater.templates.screenplay.body.markdownDescription: The Screenplay template's Body font (Template Options): all its text. Choose it in the Highwater Editor's template window too. Fonts that aren't installed print in a bundled stand-in.

highwater.templates.multiCam.body.markdownDescription: The Multi-Cam template's Body font (Template Options): all its text. Choose it in the Highwater Editor's template window too. Fonts that aren't installed print in a bundled stand-in.

highwater.templates.multiCam.uppercaseAc.markdownDescription: Multi-Cam prints action, lyrics and centred text in capitals (the Uppercase action option).

highwater.templates.manuscript.indentLea.markdownDescription: Manuscript indents every paragraph, the first after a heading or scene break too (the Indent leading paragraphs option).

highwater.templates.manuscript.spaceBefo.markdownDescription: Manuscript starts a heading that opens a page (the first, or one after `===`) a third of the way down it (the Add space before section headers option).

highwater.templates.novel.headers.markdownDescription: The Novel template's Headers font (Template Options): its headings. Choose it in the Highwater Editor's template window too. Fonts that aren't installed print in a bundled stand-in.

viewsWelcome.contents:
The Navigator, Bin, Assets, Scratchpad, Writing History and Works are in the Highwater Editor's own sidebar, at the left of the page.
[Show or Hide the Sidebar (⌘0)](command:highwater.toggleEditorSidebar)
This sidebar closes whenever you go back to the page. Switch the tab to the text editor (the code button) to use VS Code's versions of these views.

Every work in your writing history appears here, including works saved only on another computer and kept on the mirror. Save a document to start.
[Open Work from History…](command:highwater.openWorkFromHistory)

Open a .highland, .fountain or .md document to see its scenes, sections and notes, or start a new one.
[New Document…](command:highwater.newDocument)
[Open Document…](command:highwater.open)

The Bin holds text cut or copied from the script (⌥⌘X, ⌥⌘C) to use later. It is kept inside the .highland file.
[New Bin Item](command:highwater.bin.new)
[Open Scratchpad](command:highwater.openScratchpad)

The Bin holds text cut or copied from the script (⌥⌘X, ⌥⌘C) to use later. For a plain .fountain or .md file, the Bin and Scratchpad are kept with the writing history, not in the file: only Highwater Too shows them. Convert it to a .highland file to keep them in the file.
[New Bin Item](command:highwater.bin.new)
[Open Scratchpad](command:highwater.openScratchpad)
Open a document to use its Bin and Scratchpad.

Images kept inside this .highland file. Drag one into the text to show it in the manuscript.
[Add Image…](command:highwater.assets.add)

Images for this document. For a plain .fountain or .md file they go in a folder next to the file, made when you add the first one. Drag one into the text to show it in the manuscript.
[Add Image…](command:highwater.assets.add)
Open a document to add images to it.

Each save of a document is recorded here: one git repository for all your writing, with a branch per script. Open a script to see its saves, or open any work in the history, including ones saved on another computer.
[Open Work from History…](command:highwater.openWorkFromHistory)
[Change Location…](command:highwater.changeHistoryLocation)
